title.raw: 卷五十五 志第四十五 食貨五 Volume 55 Treatises 51: Finance and Economics 4

sentences.zh: 食貨五

translations.literal: Finance and Economics 5
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part Five

sentences.zh: 武德元年，文武官給祿，頗減隋制，一品七百石，從一品六百石，二品五百石，從二品四百六十石，三品四百石，從三品三百六十石，四品三百石，從四品二百六十石，五品二百石，從五品百六十石，六品百石，從六品九十石，七品八十石，從七品七十石，八品六十石，從八品五十石，九品四十石，從九品三十石，皆以歲給之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, civil and military officials were granted salaries, considerably reduced from the Sui system: rank 1a, seven hundred piculs; 1b, six hundred; 2a, five hundred; 2b, four hundred sixty; 3a, four hundred; 3b, three hundred sixty; 4a, three hundred; 4b, two hundred sixty; 5a, two hundred; 5b, one hundred sixty; 6a, one hundred; 6b, ninety; 7a, eighty; 7b, seventy; 8a, sixty; 8b, fifty; 9a, forty; 9b, thirty—all paid annually.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1 (618), the court set salaries for civil and military officials well below Sui levels: first rank received seven hundred piculs of grain per year, associate first rank six hundred, and so on down to ninth rank at forty piculs and associate ninth at thirty. All were paid once a year.

sentences.zh: 外官則否。

translations.literal: Local officials were not [included].
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and local officials were not included.

sentences.zh: 一品有職分田十二頃，二品十頃，三品九頃，四品七頃，五品六頃，六品四頃，七品三頃，五十畝，八品二頃五十畝，九品二頃，皆給百里內之地。

translations.literal: Rank 1a received twelve qing of office land; 2a, ten qing; 3a, nine; 4a, seven; 5a, six; 6a, four; 7a, three qing and fifty mu; 8a, two qing and fifty mu; 9a, two qing—all allotted within one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials of first rank received twelve qing of office land, second rank ten qing, and so on through ninth rank at two qing; seventh rank received three qing plus fifty mu, eighth rank two qing and fifty mu. All land was assigned within a radius of one hundred li.

sentences.zh: 諸州都督、都護、親王府官二品十二頃，三品十頃，四品八頃，五品七頃，六品五頃，七品四頃，八品三頃，九品二頃五十畝。

translations.literal: For regional inspectors, protectors-general, and princely household officials: 2a, twelve qing; 3a, ten; 4a, eight; 5a, seven; 6a, five; 7a, four; 8a, three; 9a, two qing and fifty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Regional inspectors, protectors-general, and officials of princely establishments received office land by rank: second rank twelve qing, third ten, fourth eight, fifth seven, sixth five, seventh four, eighth three, and ninth two qing and fifty mu.

sentences.zh: 鎮戍、關津、嶽瀆官五品五頃，六品三頃五十畝，七品三頃，八品二頃，九品一頃五十畝。

translations.literal: Garrison, pass, and sacred-mountain officials: 5a, five qing; 6a, three qing and fifty mu; 7a, three qing; 8a, two qing; 9a, one qing and fifty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at frontier garrisons, passes and ferries, and sacred mountains received five qing at fifth rank, three qing and fifty mu at sixth, three qing at seventh, two at eighth, and one qing and fifty mu at ninth.

sentences.zh: 三衛中郎將、上府折沖都尉六頃，中府五頃五十畝，下府及郎將五頃；

translations.literal: Central Guard lieutenant generals and chief commandants of superior prefectures, six qing; of middle prefectures, five qing and fifty mu; of inferior prefectures and commandant-lieutenants, five qing;
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant generals of the Three Guards and chief commandants of superior military prefectures received six qing; those of middle prefectures five qing and fifty mu; those of inferior prefectures and commandant-lieutenants five qing;

sentences.zh: 上府果毅都尉四頃，中府三頃五十畝，下府三頃；

translations.literal: Assistant commandants of superior prefectures, four qing; of middle prefectures, three qing and fifty mu; of inferior prefectures, three qing;
translations.idiomatic: Assistant commandants of superior prefectures received four qing; of middle prefectures three qing and fifty mu; of inferior prefectures three qing;

sentences.zh: 上府長史、別將三頃，中府、下府二頃五十畝；

translations.literal: Chiefs of staff and deputy generals of superior prefectures, three qing; of middle and inferior prefectures, two qing and fifty mu;
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs of staff and deputy generals of superior prefectures received three qing; those of middle and inferior prefectures two qing and fifty mu;

sentences.zh: 親王府典軍五頃五十畝，副典軍四頃；

translations.literal: Princely household commandants, five qing and fifty mu; deputy commandants, four qing;
translations.idiomatic: Commandants of princely households received five qing and fifty mu; deputy commandants four qing;

sentences.zh: 千牛備身左右、太子千牛備身三頃；

translations.literal: Left and right Gentlemen-at-Arms of the Thousand-Ox Guard and Crown Prince Gentlemen-at-Arms, three qing;
translations.idiomatic: Left and right Gentlemen-at-Arms of the Thousand-Ox Guard and those attached to the Crown Prince received three qing each;

sentences.zh: 折沖上府兵曹二頃，中府、下府一頃五十畝。

translations.literal: Military aides of superior prefectures, two qing; of middle and inferior prefectures, one qing and fifty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Military aides of superior military prefectures received two qing; those of middle and inferior prefectures one qing and fifty mu.

sentences.zh: 外軍校尉一頃二十畝，旅帥一頃，隊正、副八十畝。

translations.literal: Field company commanders, one qing and twenty mu; brigade leaders, one qing; squad leaders and deputies, eighty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Field company commanders received one qing and twenty mu; brigade leaders one qing; squad leaders and their deputies eighty mu.

sentences.zh: 親王以下又有永業田百頃，職事官一品六十頃，郡王、職事官從一品五十頃，國公、職事官從二品三十五頃，縣公、職事官三品二十五頃，職事官從三品二十頃，侯、職事官四品十二頃，子、職事官五品八頃，男、職事官從五品五頃，六品、七品二頃五十畝，八品、九品二頃。

translations.literal: Below princes there was also perpetual-heritage land: princes, one hundred qing; substantive officials 1a, sixty; commandery princes and substantive 1b, fifty; state dukes and substantive 2b, thirty-five; county dukes and substantive 3a, twenty-five; substantive 3b, twenty; marquises and substantive 4a, twelve; viscounts and substantive 5a, eight; barons and substantive 5b, five; ranks 6–7, two qing and fifty mu; ranks 8–9, two qing.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and below also held perpetual-heritage estates: a full prince one hundred qing; a substantive first-rank official sixty; a commandery prince or substantive associate first rank fifty; a state duke or substantive associate second rank thirty-five; and so on down to sixth and seventh ranks at two qing and fifty mu and eighth and ninth at two qing.

sentences.zh: 上柱國三十頃，柱國二十五頃，上護軍二十頃，護軍十五頃，上輕車都尉十頃，輕車都尉七頃，上騎都尉六頃，騎都尉四頃，驍騎、飛騎尉八十畝，雲騎、武騎尉六十畝。

translations.literal: Senior Pillar of State, thirty qing; Pillar of State, twenty-five; Senior Guardian General, twenty; Guardian General, fifteen; Senior Commandant of Light Chariots, ten; Commandant of Light Chariots, seven; Senior Commandant of Cavalry, six; Commandant of Cavalry, four; Commandants of Valiant and Flying Cavalry, eighty mu; Commandants of Cloud and Martial Cavalry, sixty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Honorary ranks carried land grants as well: Senior Pillar of State thirty qing, Pillar of State twenty-five, Senior Guardian General twenty, Guardian General fifteen, and on down to Commandants of Valiant and Flying Cavalry at eighty mu and Commandants of Cloud and Martial Cavalry at sixty.

sentences.zh: 散官五品以上給同職事官。

translations.literal: Honorary officials of fifth rank and above received the same as substantive officials.
translations.idiomatic: Honorary officials from fifth rank upward received the same allotments as substantive officials of the same grade.

sentences.zh: 五品以上受田寬鄉，六品以下受於本鄉。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above received land in broad districts; sixth rank and below in their home district.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fifth rank and above drew land from districts with surplus acreage; those of sixth rank and below from their own home districts.

sentences.zh: 解免者追田，除名者受口分之田，襲爵者不別給。

translations.literal: Those dismissed had land reclaimed; those struck from the rolls received personal-share land; heirs who succeeded to titles received no separate grant.
translations.idiomatic: When an official was removed from office his land was taken back; when his name was struck from the rolls he kept only personal-share land; a son who inherited a noble title received no additional grant.

sentences.zh: 流內九品以上口分田終其身，六十以上停私乃收。

translations.literal: For exiles within the realm of ninth rank and above, personal-share land lasted their lifetime; after age sixty they ceased private use and it was reclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Exiled officials of ninth rank and above kept personal-share land for life; after they turned sixty private use ceased and the land reverted to the state.

sentences.zh: 凡給田而無地者，畝給粟二斗。

translations.literal: Whenever land was allotted but no land was available, two dou of grain per mu were given.
translations.idiomatic: When an official was entitled to land but none could be assigned, the state paid two dou of grain per mu in lieu.

sentences.zh: 京司及州縣皆有公廨田，供公私之費。

translations.literal: The capital offices and prefectures and counties all had office-compound land to meet public and private expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Capital departments and local governments alike held office-compound land to cover official expenses.

sentences.zh: 其後以用度不足，京官有俸賜而巳。

translations.literal: Later, because expenditures were insufficient, capital officials received only salary grants.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as costs outran revenue, capital officials received only cash salaries and grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 諸司置公廨本錢，以番官貿易取息，計員多少為月料。

translations.literal: Each office set up office-capital funds; rotating clerks traded to collect interest, and monthly allowances were fixed according to staff numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Departments established office-capital funds and assigned clerks in rotation to trade on the principal; monthly allowances were apportioned by headcount.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，百官得上考者，給祿一季。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, officials who received a top evaluation were granted one season's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era, officials rated 'superior' in annual review received an extra quarter's salary.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又詔得上下考給祿一年，出使者稟其家，新至官者計日給糧。

translations.literal: Before long, it was further ordered that those with upper or lower 'superior' ratings receive one year's salary; envoys were provisioned at home, and newly arrived officials received grain by the day.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict extended the bonus to officials rated either 'superior' or 'lower superior,' granting a full year's salary; envoys drew rations for their households, and newcomers were paid grain by the day until regular salary began.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人高季輔言：「外官卑品貧匱，宜給祿養親。」

translations.literal: Zhongshu Sheren Gao Jifu said: 'Low-ranking local officials are poor and should receive salaries to support their parents.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jifu, Attendant Drafting the Secretariat, urged: 'Junior provincial officials are destitute; they ought to receive salaries to support their families.'

sentences.zh: 自後以地租春秋給京官，歲凡五十萬一千五百余斛。

translations.literal: Thereafter land tax was paid spring and autumn to capital officials, totaling more than 501,500 hu per year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter land tax from the circuits was delivered to capital officials in spring and autumn, about 501,500 hu annually.

sentences.zh: 外官降京官一等，一品以五十石為一等，二品、三品以三十石為一等，四品、五品以二十石為一等，六品、七品以五石為一等，八品、九品以二石五斗為一等。

translations.literal: Local officials were one grade below capital officials: 1a by increments of fifty piculs; 2a and 3a by thirty; 4a and 5a by twenty; 6a and 7a by five; 8a and 9a by two piculs and five dou.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial salaries stood one grade below capital rates: first rank advanced in steps of fifty piculs; second and third in steps of thirty; fourth and fifth of twenty; sixth and seventh of five; eighth and ninth of two piculs and five dou.

sentences.zh: 無粟則以鹽為祿。

translations.literal: When grain was unavailable, salt was given as salary.
translations.idiomatic: Where grain could not be delivered, salt was paid in its place.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以職田侵漁百姓，詔給逃還貧戶，視職田多少，每畝給粟二升，謂之「地子」。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, because office land encroached on the people, an edict granted it to returned refugees and poor households; according to the amount of office land, two sheng of grain per mu were given, called 'land seed.'
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven, because officials' office land had encroached on commoners, the court ordered it returned to refugees and the poor; for each mu of office land reclaimed, two sheng of grain per mu was paid as compensation, called the 'land seed' payment.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以水旱復罷之。

translations.literal: That year, because of flood and drought it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That same year flood and drought forced the measure to be revoked.

sentences.zh: 十二年，罷諸司公廨本錢，以天下上戶七千人為胥士，視防閤制而收其課，計官多少而給之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, office-capital funds of all offices were abolished; seven thousand top households empire-wide were made retainers; following the household-guard system their dues were collected and distributed according to official numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve the office-capital funds were abolished and seven thousand wealthy households empire-wide were enrolled as retainers; their dues, collected on the model of household guards, funded allowances apportioned by rank.

sentences.zh: 十五年，復置公廨本錢，以諸司令史主之，號「捉錢令史」。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, office-capital funds were restored, managed by clerks of each office, called 'money-handling clerks.'
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen office-capital funds were restored under clerks of each department, titled 'money-handling clerks.'

sentences.zh: 每司九人，補於吏部，所主才五萬錢以下，市肆販易，月納息錢四千，歲滿受官。

translations.literal: Nine per office, appointed by the Ministry of Personnel; each managed no more than fifty thousand cash, traded in markets, paid four thousand cash interest monthly, and after one year received office.
translations.idiomatic: Each department had nine such clerks, appointed by the Ministry of Personnel; each handled capital of fifty thousand cash or less, traded in the markets, paid four thousand cash in monthly interest, and after a year qualified for regular office.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫褚遂良上疏：「京七十余司，更一二載，捉錢令史六百余人受職。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Chu Suiliang memorialized: 'In the capital's more than seventy offices, within another year or two more than six hundred money-handling clerks will receive posts.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang, Grandee Remonstrator, memorialized: 'Within a year or two more than six hundred money-handling clerks across the capital's seventy-odd departments will have bought their way into office.

sentences.zh: 太學高第，諸州進士，拔十取五，猶有犯禁罹法者，況廛肆之人，茍得無恥，不可使其居職。」

translations.literal: Top graduates of the Imperial Academy and presented scholars from the provinces, chosen five from ten, still have violators of prohibitions and law—how much more shopkeepers, who are shameless if they can gain, and must not be allowed to hold office.'
translations.idiomatic: Even among top Academy graduates and provincial candidates, chosen at a rate of five in ten, some still break the law—how much less market traders, who will stoop to anything for profit and must never be allowed to serve as officials.'

sentences.zh: 太宗乃罷捉錢令史，復詔給百官俸。

translations.literal: Taizong then abolished money-handling clerks and again ordered salaries paid to all officials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong abolished the money-handling clerks and restored regular salaries for the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以京兆府、岐、同、華、邠、坊州隙地陂澤可墾者，復給京官職田。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, idle land, marshes, and reclaimable plots in Jingzhao prefecture and Qi, Tong, Hua, Bin, and Fang prefectures were again granted as capital officials' office land.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen reclaimable waste and marshland in Jingzhao and the prefectures of Qi, Tong, Hua, Bin, and Fang was again assigned as office land for capital officials.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，置京諸司公廨本錢，捉以令史、府史、胥士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, office-capital funds for capital offices were established, managed by clerks, prefectural clerks, and retainers.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two capital departments again received office-capital funds, managed by department clerks, prefectural clerks, and retainers.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，廢之，以天下租腳直為京官俸料。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui it was abolished; empire-wide transport surcharges on rent were used for capital officials' salary provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 1 (650) the funds were abolished and empire-wide transport surcharges on land tax were devoted to capital salaries.

sentences.zh: 其後又薄斂一歲稅，以高戶主之，月收息給俸。

translations.literal: Later a light levy of one year's tax was again imposed, managed by wealthy households, with monthly interest collected for salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court again levied a reduced year's tax, entrusted to wealthy households, whose monthly interest payments funded salaries.

sentences.zh: 尋顓以稅錢給之，歲總十五萬二千七百三十緡。

translations.literal: Soon the entire tax money was used for payment; the annual total was 152,730 strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the full tax proceeds were paid out directly, totaling 152,730 strings of cash per year.

sentences.zh: 一品月俸八千，食料一千八百，雜用一千二百。

translations.literal: Rank 1a: monthly salary eight thousand, food allowance one thousand eight hundred, miscellaneous one thousand two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: First rank: eight thousand cash monthly salary, eighteen hundred for food, twelve hundred for miscellaneous expenses.

sentences.zh: 二品月俸六千五百，食料一千五百，雜用一千。

translations.literal: Rank 2a: monthly salary six thousand five hundred, food allowance one thousand five hundred, miscellaneous one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank: six thousand five hundred cash salary, fifteen hundred for food, one thousand miscellaneous.

sentences.zh: 三品月俸五千一百，雜用九百。

translations.literal: Rank 3a: monthly salary five thousand one hundred, miscellaneous nine hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank: five thousand one hundred cash salary and nine hundred miscellaneous.

sentences.zh: 四品月俸三千五百，食料、雜用七百。

translations.literal: Rank 4a: monthly salary three thousand five hundred, food and miscellaneous seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank: three thousand five hundred cash salary plus seven hundred for food and miscellaneous.

sentences.zh: 五品月俸三千，食料、雜用六百。

translations.literal: Rank 5a: monthly salary three thousand, food and miscellaneous six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: three thousand cash salary plus six hundred for food and miscellaneous.

sentences.zh: 六品月俸二千，食料、雜用四百。

translations.literal: Rank 6a: monthly salary two thousand, food and miscellaneous four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank: two thousand cash salary plus four hundred for food and miscellaneous.

sentences.zh: 七品月俸一千七百五十，食料、雜用三百五十。

translations.literal: Rank 7a: monthly salary one thousand seven hundred fifty, food and miscellaneous three hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh rank: one thousand seven hundred fifty cash salary plus three hundred fifty for food and miscellaneous.

sentences.zh: 八品月俸一千三百，食料三百，雜用二百五十。

translations.literal: Rank 8a: monthly salary one thousand three hundred, food three hundred, miscellaneous two hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth rank: thirteen hundred cash salary, three hundred for food, two hundred fifty miscellaneous.

sentences.zh: 九品月俸一千五十，食料二百五十，雜用二百。

translations.literal: Rank 9a: monthly salary one thousand fifty, food two hundred fifty, miscellaneous two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth rank: one thousand fifty cash salary, two hundred fifty for food, two hundred miscellaneous.

sentences.zh: 行署月俸一百四十，食料三十。

translations.literal: Traveling offices: monthly salary one hundred forty, food thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile branch offices: one hundred forty cash monthly salary and thirty for food.

sentences.zh: 職事官又有防閤、庶仆：一品防閤九十六人，二品七十二人，三品四十八人，四品三十二人，五品二十四人；

translations.literal: Substantive officials also had household guards and general servants: 1a, ninety-six guards; 2a, seventy-two; 3a, forty-eight; 4a, thirty-two; 5a, twenty-four;
translations.idiomatic: Substantive officials also received household guards and general servants: first rank ninety-six guards, second seventy-two, third forty-eight, fourth thirty-two, fifth twenty-four;

sentences.zh: 六品庶仆十五人，七品四人，八品三人，九品二人。

translations.literal: 6a, fifteen general servants; 7a, four; 8a, three; 9a, two.
translations.idiomatic: sixth rank fifteen general servants, seventh four, eighth three, ninth two.

sentences.zh: 公主有邑士八十人，郡主六十人，縣主四十人。

translations.literal: Imperial princesses had eighty fief retainers; commandery princesses, sixty; county princesses, forty.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princesses received eighty fief retainers, commandery princesses sixty, and county princesses forty.

sentences.zh: 外官以州、府、縣上下中為差，少尹、長史、司馬及丞減長官之半，參軍、博士減判司三之二，主簿、縣尉減丞三之二，錄事、市令以參軍職田為輕重，京縣錄事以縣尉職田為輕重。

translations.literal: Local officials differed by whether prefecture, prefectural city, or county was upper, lower, or middle; vice-prefects, chiefs of staff, aides, and assistants received half the chief's allotment; aides and erudites two-thirds of the administrator's; recorders and market chiefs by the aide's office land; capital-county recorders by the county captain's.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial allotments varied with whether a prefecture, subprefecture, or county was rated upper, middle, or lower; deputies, chiefs of staff, aides, and assistants received half the chief's grant; military aides and erudites two-thirds of the administrator's; recorders and market superintendents followed the aide's scale, and recorders in capital counties the county captain's.

sentences.zh: 羈縻州官，給以土物。

translations.literal: Officials of tethered prefectures were given local products.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of subordinate 'tethered' prefectures were paid in local goods.

sentences.zh: 關監官，給以年支輕貨。

translations.literal: Pass and market officials were given annual light goods.
translations.idiomatic: Pass and customs officials received lightweight goods for annual expenses.

sentences.zh: 折沖府官則有仗身：上府折沖都尉六人，果毅四人，長史、別將三人，兵曹二人，中、下府各減一人，皆十五日而代。

translations.literal: Military prefecture officials had armed attendants: superior prefecture chief commandant six, assistant commandant four, chief of staff and deputy general three, military aide two; middle and inferior prefectures each reduced by one; all rotated every fifteen days.
translations.idiomatic: Military prefecture officials had armed attendants: a chief commandant of a superior prefecture six, an assistant commandant four, chief of staff and deputy general three, military aide two—each reduced by one in middle and inferior prefectures—all rotating every fifteen days.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司、特進、光祿大夫同職事官，公廨、雜用不給。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor of the Palace with Three Insignia, Special Advancement, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness equaled substantive officials; office and miscellaneous were not given.
translations.idiomatic: Honorary grandees such as Grand Preceptor of the Palace with Three Insignia, Special Advancement, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness ranked with substantive officials but received no office funds or miscellaneous allowances.

sentences.zh: 員外官、檢校、判、試、知給祿料食糧之半，散官、勛官、衛官減四之一，致仕五品以上給半祿，解官充侍亦如之。

translations.literal: Supernumerary, acting, provisional, trial, and concurrent officials received half salary provisions and grain; honorary, merit, and guard officials were reduced one-fourth; retired fifth rank and above received half salary; dismissed officials serving as attendants likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary, acting, provisional, trial, and concurrent officials received half salary and grain; honorary, merit, and guard officials three-quarters; retirees of fifth rank and above half pay; and dismissed officials serving as attendants the same.

sentences.zh: 四夷宿衛同京官。

translations.literal: Barbarian palace guards equaled capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Foreigners serving as palace guards received the same treatment as capital officials.

sentences.zh: 天下置公廨本錢，以典史主之，收贏十之七，以供佐史以下不賦粟者常食，余為百官俸料。

translations.literal: Empire-wide office-capital funds were established, managed by record clerks; seven-tenths of profit was collected to supply regular food for aides and below who received no grain, the remainder for officials' salary provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Office-capital funds were set up throughout the empire under record clerks; seven-tenths of the interest fed aides and clerks who received no grain salary, and the rest funded official pay.

sentences.zh: 京兆、河南府錢三百八十萬，太原及四大都督府二百七十五萬，中都督府、上州二百四十二萬，下都督、中州一百五十四萬，下州八十八萬；

translations.literal: Jingzhao and Henan prefectures, 3,800,000 cash; Taiyuan and the four great area commands, 2,750,000; middle area commands and upper prefectures, 2,420,000; lower area commands and middle prefectures, 1,540,000; lower prefectures, 880,000;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao and Henan each held 3.8 million cash; Taiyuan and the four great area commands 2.75 million; middle commands and upper prefectures 2.42 million; lower commands and middle prefectures 1.54 million; lower prefectures 880,000;

sentences.zh: 京兆、河南府京縣一百四十三萬，太原府京縣九十一萬三千，京兆、河南府畿縣八十二萬五千，太原府畿縣、諸州上縣七十七萬，中縣五十五萬，中下縣、下縣三十八萬五千；

translations.literal: Capital counties of Jingzhao and Henan, 1,430,000; capital counties of Taiyuan, 913,000; metropolitan counties of Jingzhao and Henan, 825,000; metropolitan counties of Taiyuan and upper counties of prefectures, 770,000; middle counties, 550,000; lower-middle and lower counties, 385,000;
translations.idiomatic: capital counties of Jingzhao and Henan 1.43 million; capital counties of Taiyuan 913,000; metropolitan counties of Jingzhao and Henan 825,000; metropolitan counties of Taiyuan and upper counties elsewhere 770,000; middle counties 550,000; lower-middle and lower counties 385,000;

sentences.zh: 折沖上府二十萬，中府減四之一，下府十萬。

translations.literal: Superior military prefectures, 200,000; middle prefectures reduced one-fourth; inferior prefectures, 100,000.
translations.idiomatic: superior military prefectures 200,000 cash; middle prefectures three-quarters of that; inferior prefectures 100,000.

sentences.zh: 麟德二年，給文官五品以上仗身，以掌閑、幕士為之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Linde, armed attendants were granted to civil officials of fifth rank and above, drawn from idle laborers and tent guards.
translations.idiomatic: In Linde 2 (665) civil officials of fifth rank and above received armed attendants drawn from idle laborers and tent guards.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，與職事官皆罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng, they were abolished together with substantive officials' [benefits].
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng 1 (670) these benefits were abolished for substantive officials as well.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年，京文武官視職事品給防閤、庶仆。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng, capital civil and military officials received household guards and general servants according to substantive rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfeng 1 (666) capital civil and military officials again received household guards and servants according to substantive rank.

sentences.zh: 百官俸出於租調，運送之費甚廣。

translations.literal: Officials' salaries came from rent and corvée; transport costs were very great.
translations.idiomatic: Official salaries were drawn from land tax and corvée levies, and transport costs were enormous.

sentences.zh: 公廨出舉，典史有徹垣墉、鬻田宅以免責者。

translations.literal: Office funds were lent out; record clerks tore down walls and sold fields and houses to escape liability.
translations.idiomatic: When office funds were lent at interest, record clerks sometimes demolished walls and sold property to escape debt.

sentences.zh: 又以雜職供薪炭，納直倍於正丁。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous laborers were also used for fuel; the fee paid was double that of regular adult males.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous laborers were also levied for fuel, paying twice the commutation fee of regular adult males.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年，王公以下率口出錢，以充百官俸食防閤、庶仆、邑士、仗身、封戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yifeng, princes and dukes and below were levied per capita to fund officials' salaries, food, household guards, general servants, fief retainers, armed attendants, and fief households.
translations.idiomatic: In Yifeng 3 (678) princes, dukes, and commoners alike were taxed per capita to fund salaries, food, guards, servants, fief retainers, armed attendants, and enfeoffed households.

sentences.zh: 調露元年，職事五品以上復給仗身。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiaolu, substantive officials of fifth rank and above again received armed attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiaolu 1 (679) substantive officials of fifth rank and above again received armed attendants.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，以京官八品、九品俸薄，詔八品歲給庶仆三人，九品二人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzai, because capital officials of ranks 8a and 9a had thin salaries, an edict granted 8a three general servants yearly and 9a two.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangzai 1 (684), because eighth- and ninth-rank capital officials were poorly paid, the court granted eighth rank three general servants per year and ninth rank two.

sentences.zh: 文武職事三品以上給親事、帳內。

translations.literal: Civil and military substantive officials of third rank and above were given personal attendants and tent guards.
translations.idiomatic: Substantive civil and military officials of third rank and above received personal attendants and tent guards.

sentences.zh: 以六品、七品子為親事，以八品、九品子為帳內，歲納錢千五百，謂之「品子課錢」。

translations.literal: Sons of sixth- and seventh-rank officials served as personal attendants; sons of eighth- and ninth-rank as tent guards; they paid fifteen hundred cash yearly, called 'rank-son duty money.'
translations.idiomatic: Sons of sixth- and seventh-rank officials served as personal attendants and sons of eighth- and ninth-rank as tent guards, each paying fifteen hundred cash a year in what was called 'rank-son duty money.'

sentences.zh: 三師、三公、開府儀同三司百三十人；

translations.literal: Three Preceptors, Three Dukes, and Grand Preceptors of the Palace with Three Insignia, one hundred thirty persons;
translations.idiomatic: The Three Preceptors, Three Dukes, and Grand Preceptors of the Palace with Three Insignia received one hundred thirty attendants;

sentences.zh: 嗣王、郡王百八人；

translations.literal: heirs apparent to princedoms and commandery princes, one hundred eight;
translations.idiomatic: heirs to princedoms and commandery princes, one hundred eight;

sentences.zh: 上柱國領二品以上職事九十五人，領三品職事六十九人；

translations.literal: Senior Pillar of State holding substantive office of second rank and above, ninety-five; holding third rank, sixty-nine;
translations.idiomatic: a Senior Pillar of State holding substantive second rank or above ninety-five, or third rank sixty-nine;

sentences.zh: 柱國領二品以上職事七十三人，領三品職事五十五人；

translations.literal: Pillar of State holding second rank and above substantive office, seventy-three; third rank, fifty-five;
translations.idiomatic: a Pillar of State with substantive second rank or above seventy-three, or third rank fifty-five;

sentences.zh: 護軍領二品以上職事六十二人，領三品職事三十六人。

translations.literal: Guardian General holding second rank and above substantive office, sixty-two; third rank, thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: a Guardian General with substantive second rank or above sixty-two, or third rank thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 二品以下又有白直、執衣：二品白直四十人，三品三十二人，四品二十四人，五品十六人，六品十人，七品七人，八品五人，九品四人；

translations.literal: Second rank and below also had white-clad runners and robe-bearers: 2a, forty white-clad; 3a, thirty-two; 4a, twenty-four; 5a, sixteen; 6a, ten; 7a, seven; 8a, five; 9a, four;
translations.idiomatic: Officials of second rank and below also had white-clad runners and robe-bearers: second rank forty runners, third thirty-two, fourth twenty-four, fifth sixteen, sixth ten, seventh seven, eighth five, ninth four;

sentences.zh: 二品執衣十八人，三品十五人，四品十三人，五品九人，六品、七品各六人，八品、九品各三人。

translations.literal: 2a, eighteen robe-bearers; 3a, fifteen; 4a, thirteen; 5a, nine; 6a and 7a, six each; 8a and 9a, three each.
translations.idiomatic: second rank eighteen robe-bearers, third fifteen, fourth thirteen, fifth nine, sixth and seventh six each, eighth and ninth three each.

sentences.zh: 皆中男為之。

translations.literal: All were drawn from middle youths.
translations.idiomatic: All were drawn from youths of middle age.

sentences.zh: 防閤、庶仆，皆滿歲而代。

translations.literal: Household guards and general servants all rotated at year's end.
translations.idiomatic: Household guards and general servants all rotated once a year.

sentences.zh: 外官五品以上亦有執衣。

translations.literal: Local officials of fifth rank and above also had robe-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials of fifth rank and above also received robe-bearers.

sentences.zh: 都護府不治州事亦有仗身：都護四人，副都護、長史、司馬三人，諸曹參軍事二人，上鎮將四人，中下鎮將、上鎮副三人，中、下鎮副各二人，鎮倉曹、關令丞、戍主副各一人，皆取於防人衛士，十五日而代。

translations.literal: Protectorates that did not administer prefectures also had armed attendants: protector four, vice-protector, chief of staff, and aide three each, bureau aides two, superior garrison commandant four, middle and inferior commandants and superior deputy three, middle and inferior deputies two each, garrison granary clerk, pass magistrate's aide, and frontier post deputy one each—all from garrison guards, rotating every fifteen days.
translations.idiomatic: Even protectorates that did not govern regular prefectures had armed attendants: the protector four, his deputy, chief of staff, and aide three each, bureau aides two, and so on down to frontier post deputies—all drawn from garrison guards and rotating every fifteen days.

sentences.zh: 宿衛官三品以上仗身三人，五品以上二人，六品以下及散官五品以上各一人，取於番上衛士，役而不收課。

translations.literal: Palace guard officials of third rank and above, three armed attendants; fifth rank and above, two; sixth rank and below and honorary fifth rank and above, one each—drawn from rotating palace guards, serving without paying duty money.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guard officials of third rank and above had three armed attendants, fifth rank and above two, sixth and below and honorary fifth rank and above one each—drawn from rotating guards who served without paying commutation fees.

sentences.zh: 親王出籓者，府佐史、典軍、副典軍有事力人，數如白直。

translations.literal: Princes who went out to their fiefs: household aides, commandants, and deputy commandants had laborers in numbers like white-clad runners.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial princes went out to their fiefs, their household aides, commandants, and deputies received laborers in the same numbers as white-clad runners.

sentences.zh: 諸司、諸使有守當及廳子，以兵及勛官為之。

translations.literal: All offices and commissioners had guards and hall attendants, drawn from soldiers and merit officials.
translations.idiomatic: Departments and special commissioners had guards and hall attendants drawn from soldiers and merit officials.

sentences.zh: 白直、執衣以下分三番，周歲而代，供役不逾境。

translations.literal: White-clad runners, robe-bearers, and below were divided in three shifts, rotating yearly; service did not cross borders.
translations.idiomatic: White-clad runners, robe-bearers, and below served in three rotating shifts, replaced yearly, and did not serve outside their district.

sentences.zh: 後皆納課：仗身錢六百四十，防閤、庶仆、白直錢二千五百，執衣錢一千。

translations.literal: Later all paid duty money: armed attendant money six hundred forty; household guard, general servant, and white-clad money two thousand five hundred; robe-bearer money one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Later all paid commutation fees instead: six hundred forty cash for an armed attendant, twenty-five hundred for a guard, servant, or white-clad runner, one thousand for a robe-bearer.

sentences.zh: 其後親事、帳內亦納課如品子之數。

translations.literal: Later personal attendants and tent guards also paid duty like rank-sons.
translations.idiomatic: Later personal attendants and tent guards also paid the same commutation as rank-sons.

sentences.zh: 州縣典史捉公廨本錢者，收利十之七。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county record clerks who handled office-capital funds collected seven-tenths of the profit.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county clerks who managed office-capital funds kept seven-tenths of the interest.

sentences.zh: 富戶幸免徭役，貧者破產甚眾。

translations.literal: Wealthy households escaped corvée; many poor went bankrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households escaped corvée while many poor families were ruined.

sentences.zh: 秘書少監崔沔請計戶均出，每丁加升尺，所增蓋少；

translations.literal: Secretariat Vice Director Cui Mian requested apportionment by household, adding a sheng and chi per adult male—the increase would be slight;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Mian, Vice Director of the Secretariat, urged spreading the burden by household with a small surcharge per adult male;

sentences.zh: 流亡漸復，倉庫充實，然後取於正賦，罷新加者。

translations.literal: as refugees gradually returned and granaries filled, then take from regular tax and abolish the new surcharge.
translations.idiomatic: and once refugees returned and granaries were full, fund salaries from regular tax and abolish the surcharge.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，中書舍人張嘉貞又陳其不便，遂罷天下公廨本錢，復稅戶以給百官；

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, Zhongshu Sheren Zhang Jiazhen again stated its inconvenience; empire-wide office-capital funds were abolished and taxpayers again supplied all officials;
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 10 (722) Zhang Jiazhen, Attendant Drafting the Secretariat, again protested the system; empire-wide office-capital funds were abolished and taxpayers again funded the bureaucracy;

sentences.zh: 籍內外職田，賦逃還戶及貧民；

translations.literal: office land inside and outside the capital was registered and assigned to returned refugees and the poor;
translations.idiomatic: office land inside and outside the capital was registered and assigned to returned refugees and the poor;

sentences.zh: 罷職事五品以上仗身。

translations.literal: Abolished zhangshen for office-holding officials of fifth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: Armed personal attendants for active officials of fifth rank and above were abolished.

sentences.zh: 十八年，復給京官職田。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, capital officials' office land was again granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 18 (730), the court restored office-land allotments to capital officials.

sentences.zh: 州縣籍一歲稅錢為本，以高戶捉之，月收贏以給外官。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties registered one year's tax money as capital, assigned wealthy households to manage it, and each month collected profit to supply local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties set aside one year's tax revenue as seed capital, entrusted it to wealthy households for lending, and used the monthly interest to pay provincial officials.

sentences.zh: 復置天下公廨本錢，收贏十之六。

translations.literal: Again established empire-wide office-capital funds, taking six-tenths of the profit.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide office-capital funds were reinstated, with the state claiming sixty percent of the interest.

sentences.zh: 十九年，初置職田頃畝簿，租價無過六斗，地不毛者畝給二斗。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, an acreage register for office land was first established; rent price was not to exceed six dou, and for non-fertile land two dou per mu were allotted.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 19 the court introduced a registry of office-land holdings in qing and mu; rents were capped at six dou, with only two dou per mu on poor soil.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，令百官防閤、庶仆俸食雜用以月給之，總稱月俸：一品錢三萬一千，二品二萬四千，三品萬七千，四品萬一千五百六十七，五品九千二百，六品五千三百，七品四千一百，八品二千四百七十五，九品千九百一十七。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, it was ordered that all officials' guard stewards, household servants, food stipends, and miscellaneous expenses be paid monthly, collectively called monthly salary: rank 1a, thirty-one thousand cash; 2a, twenty-four thousand; 3a, seventeen thousand; 4a, eleven thousand five hundred sixty-seven; 5a, nine thousand two hundred; 6a, five thousand three hundred; 7a, four thousand one hundred; 8a, two thousand four hundred seventy-five; 9a, one thousand nine hundred seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 24 (736) the court fixed monthly salaries covering guard stewards, household servants, food, and incidentals for the whole bureaucracy: first rank thirty-one thousand cash, second twenty-four thousand, third seventeen thousand, fourth eleven thousand five hundred sixty-seven, fifth nine thousand two hundred, sixth five thousand three hundred, seventh four thousand one hundred, eighth two thousand four hundred seventy-five, and ninth one thousand nine hundred seventeen.

sentences.zh: 祿米則歲再給之：一品七百斛，從一品六百斛，二品五百斛，從二品四百六十斛，三品四百斛，從三品三百六十斛，四品三百斛，從四品二百五十斛，五品二百斛，從五品百六十斛，六品百斛，自此十斛為率，至從七品七十斛，八品六十七斛，自此五斛為率，至從九品五十二斛。

translations.literal: Salary grain was then given twice a year: 1a, seven hundred piculs; 1b, six hundred; 2a, five hundred; 2b, four hundred sixty; 3a, four hundred; 3b, three hundred sixty; 4a, three hundred; 4b, two hundred fifty; 5a, two hundred; 5b, one hundred sixty; 6a, one hundred; from here ten piculs as the rate, down to 7b at seventy; 8a, sixty-seven; from here five piculs as the rate, down to 9b at fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Grain salaries were paid twice yearly: seven hundred piculs for first rank, six hundred for associate first rank, and so on through sixth rank at one hundred piculs; from sixth rank downward the allotment fell by ten piculs per step to associate seventh rank at seventy, then by five piculs per step to associate ninth rank at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 外官降一等。

translations.literal: Local officials were reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials received one rank less than their capital counterparts.

sentences.zh: 先是州縣無防人者，籍十八以上中男及殘疾以守城門及倉庫門，謂之門夫。

translations.literal: Previously, where prefectures and counties lacked guard personnel, able-bodied males eighteen and above and the disabled were registered to guard city gates and granary gates, called gate keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, counties without standing guards had enrolled able-bodied men over eighteen and the disabled to watch city and granary gates; these men were called gate keepers.

sentences.zh: 番上不至者，閑月督課，為錢百七十，忙月二百。

translations.literal: Those who failed to report for rotation were assessed in idle months one hundred seventy cash, in busy months two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Gate keepers who missed their turn of duty were fined one hundred seventy cash in slack months and two hundred in peak months.

sentences.zh: 至是以門夫資課給州縣官。

translations.literal: At this time gate-keeper labor assessments were used to supply prefecture and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: These gate-keeper fines were now applied to the salaries of prefectural and county officials.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以京畿地狹，計丁給田猶不足，於是分諸司官在都者，給職田於都畿，以京師地給貧民。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, because the capital region's land was narrow and per-capita allotments were still insufficient, officials of various bureaus stationed in the capital were divided off; office land was granted in the capital districts, and capital land was given to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 29 (741), with the capital region overcrowded and per-capita land still inadequate, officials of central agencies were reassigned: those in the capital received office land in the surrounding districts, freeing metropolitan fields for poor households.

sentences.zh: 是時河南、北職田兼稅桑，有詔公廨、職田有桑者，毋督絲課。

translations.literal: At this time office land in Henan and Hebei also taxed mulberry; an edict stated that where office halls and office land had mulberry, silk levies were not to be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Office land in Henan and Hebei then also carried mulberry taxes, until an edict exempted any office or office-land plot bearing mulberry trees from silk assessments.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，給員外郎料，天下白直歲役丁十萬，有詔罷之，計數加稅以供用，人皆以為便。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, acting vice-ministers were granted stipends; empire-wide white-duty annual corvée laborers numbered one hundred thousand; an edict abolished this and added tax by count to supply expenses; people all considered it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era (742-755) acting vice-ministers received stipends, while an empire-wide corvée of one hundred thousand unpaid laborers was abolished and replaced with a head-count surcharge; the change was widely welcomed.

sentences.zh: 自開元後，置使甚眾，每使各給雜錢。

translations.literal: After Kaiyuan, commissioners were established in great number, and each commissioner was separately given miscellaneous funds.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kaiyuan reforms the court proliferated special commissioners, each with his own miscellaneous allowance.

sentences.zh: 宰相楊國忠身兼數官，堂封外月給錢百萬。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yang Guozhong personally held several offices; beyond hall seals he was monthly given one million cash.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yang Guozhong held several posts at once and, beyond his regular emoluments, received one million cash each month.

sentences.zh: 幽州平盧節度使安祿山、隴右節度使哥舒翰兼使所給，亦不下百萬。

translations.literal: Youzhou-Pinglu Military Commissioner An Lushan and Longyou Military Commissioner Geshu Han, combined commissioner stipends given, also were not less than one million.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan of Pinglu and Geshu Han of Longyou likewise drew no less than one million cash monthly from their combined commissioner appointments.

sentences.zh: 十二載，國忠以兩京百官職田送租勞民，請五十里外輸於縣倉，鬥納直二錢，百里外納直三錢，使百官就請於縣，然縣吏欺盜蓋多，而閑司有不能自直者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Guozhong, because both capitals' hundred officials' office-land rent delivery burdened the people, requested that beyond fifty li it be delivered to county granaries, two cash per dou as delivery fee within one hundred li and three beyond one hundred li, making all officials collect at the county; yet county clerks' fraud and theft were probably many, and idle offices had some who could not cover their own costs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 12 (753) Guozhong argued that delivering office-land rents burdened the populace of both capitals and proposed county granaries beyond fifty li, with a two-cash handling fee per dou within one hundred li and three beyond; officials were to collect at the county, but clerks embezzled heavily and many nominal posts could no longer pay their way.

sentences.zh: 十四載，兩京九品以上月給俸加十之二，同正員加十之一。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, both capitals' rank nine and above monthly salaries were increased by two-tenths; acting regulars increased by one-tenth.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 14 monthly salaries for officials of ninth rank and above in both capitals rose twenty percent, with acting appointees receiving a ten-percent increase.

sentences.zh: 兵興，權臣增領諸使，月給厚俸，比開元制祿數倍。

translations.literal: When warfare arose, powerful ministers added commissioner posts, monthly thick salaries given, several times the Kaiyuan system's salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Once war broke out, powerful ministers accumulated commissioner titles and drew monthly pay several times the Kaiyuan scale.

sentences.zh: 至德初，以用物不足，內外官不給料錢，郡府縣官給半祿及白直、品子課。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, because supplies were insufficient, inside and outside officials were not given stipend money; commandery, prefecture, and county officials were given half salary and white-duty and pinzi assessments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide era (756-758), shortages halted stipend payments for officials everywhere; local officials received half salary plus assessments on unpaid corvée labor and ranked youths.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，亦給外官半料及職田，京官給手力課而已。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, local officials were also given half stipends and office land; capital officials were given only hand-attendant assessments.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1 (758) provincial officials again received half stipends and office land, while capital officials got only attendant-service assessments.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，復令京官職田以時輸送，受加耗者以枉法贓論。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, capital officials' office land was again ordered delivered on schedule; those accepting added wastage were prosecuted as illegal corruption.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 1 (760) the court again required timely delivery of capital office-land rents and treated acceptance of padded wastage allowances as criminal graft.

sentences.zh: 其後籍以為軍糧矣。

translations.literal: Afterward it was registered and used for military grain.
translations.idiomatic: The rents were later requisitioned outright for army rations.

sentences.zh: 永泰末，取州縣官及折沖府官職田苗子三之一，市輕貨以賑京官。

translations.literal: Late in Yongtai, one-third of the seedlings from office land of county officials and zhechong-fu officials was taken, light goods purchased to relieve capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Yongtai (765-766) the court seized one-third of office-land seedlings from county and military-prefecture officials, sold them for light goods, and used the proceeds to support capital officials.

sentences.zh: 大歷元年，斂天下青苗錢，得錢四百九十萬緡，輸大盈庫，封太府左、右藏，鐍而不發者累歲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dali, green-sprout money was collected empire-wide, obtaining four million nine hundred thousand strings of cash, delivered to the Great Surplus Treasury; the Grand Treasury's left and right storehouses were sealed and locked, not opened for successive years.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 1 (766) the green-sprout tax yielded 4.9 million strings nationwide, deposited in the Great Surplus Treasury while the Grand Treasury's left and right vaults were sealed shut for years.

sentences.zh: 二年，復給京兆府及畿縣官職田，以三之一供軍饟。

translations.literal: In the second year, office land was again granted to Jingzhao Prefecture and capital-district county officials; one-third of it supplied military rations.
translations.idiomatic: The next year office land was restored to officials of Jingzhao and the capital districts, with one-third of the yield reserved for army provisions.

sentences.zh: 增稅青苗錢，一畝至三十。

translations.literal: The green-sprout tax was increased, reaching thirty per mu.
translations.idiomatic: The green-sprout levy was raised to thirty cash per mu.

sentences.zh: 權臣月俸有至九十萬者，刺史亦至十萬。

translations.literal: Powerful ministers' monthly salaries reached as much as nine hundred thousand; prefects also reached one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly pay for favored ministers rose as high as nine hundred thousand cash, and even prefects could draw one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 楊綰、常袞為相，增京官正員官及諸道觀察使、都團練使、副使以下料錢。

translations.literal: Yang Wan and Chang Gun served as chancellors and increased stipend money for capital regular officials and circuit observation commissioners, regional training commissioners, and deputy commissioners and below.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellors, Yang Wan and Chang Gun raised stipends for regular capital officials and for circuit commissioners, regional training commissioners, and their deputies.

sentences.zh: 初，檢校官同中書門下平章事者，月給錢十二萬。

translations.literal: Initially, acting commissioners equal to Grand Councilors of the Secretariat and Chancellery were monthly given one hundred twenty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Acting commissioners with Grand Councilor status had initially received one hundred twenty thousand cash per month.

sentences.zh: 至是戶部侍郎判度支韓滉請同正官，從高而給之。

translations.literal: At this time Household Ministry Vice Minister and Revenue Commissioner Han Huang requested equal treatment with regular commissioners, granting from the higher amount.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, Vice Minister of Revenue, then petitioned that such appointees receive the same pay as regular commissioners, at the higher rate.

sentences.zh: 文官一千八百五十四員，武官九百四十二員，月俸二十六萬緡，而增給者居三之一。

translations.literal: Civil officials numbered one thousand eight hundred fifty-four; military officials nine hundred forty-two; monthly salary two hundred sixty thousand strings, and those receiving increases constituted one-third.
translations.idiomatic: The rolls listed 1,854 civil and 942 military officials drawing 260,000 strings monthly, with one-third receiving the new supplements.

sentences.zh: 先是，州縣職田、公廨田，每歲六月以白簿上尚書省覆實；

translations.literal: Previously, prefecture and county office land and office-hall land each year in the sixth month were submitted on white registers to the Ministry of Revenue for verification;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, each June prefectures and counties filed white registers of office and office-hall land with the Ministry of Revenue for audit;

sentences.zh: 至十月輸送，則有黃籍，歲一易之。

translations.literal: by the tenth month for delivery, there was a yellow register, renewed once a year.
translations.idiomatic: by October, when rents were delivered, a yellow register was issued and replaced annually.

sentences.zh: 後不復簿上，唯授祖清望要官，而職卑者稽留不付，黃籍亦不復更矣。

translations.literal: Later registers were no longer submitted; rents were granted only to eminent high officials, while low-ranking ones were detained unpaid, and the yellow register was no longer renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Later the filings lapsed: rents went only to senior dignitaries, junior officials' payments were withheld, and the yellow register ceased to be updated.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，詔黃籍與白簿皆上有司。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended the throne, an edict ordered both yellow registers and white booklets submitted to the relevant departments.
translations.idiomatic: On Dezong's accession an edict restored submission of both yellow registers and white booklets to the proper agencies.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，復減百官料錢以助軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong, officials' stipend money was again reduced to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 3 (782) official stipends were cut again to fund the armies.

sentences.zh: 李泌為相，又增百官及畿內官月俸，復置手力資課，歲給錢六十一萬六千余緡，文官千八百九十二員，武官八百九十六員。

translations.literal: Li Bi served as chancellor and again increased monthly salaries for all officials and capital-district officials, restored hand-attendant stipend assessments, annually giving six hundred sixteen thousand-plus strings; civil officials one thousand eight hundred ninety-two; military officials eight hundred ninety-six.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Bi then restored and raised monthly pay for officials throughout the capital region, reinstated attendant-service assessments, and spent more than 616,000 strings a year on 1,892 civil and 896 military posts.

sentences.zh: 左右衛上將軍以下又有六雜給：一曰糧米，二曰鹽，三曰私馬，四曰手力，五曰隨身，六曰春冬服。

translations.literal: Left and Right Guard senior generals and below also had six miscellaneous grants: first, grain and rice; second, salt; third, private horses; fourth, hand attendants; fifth, personal guard; sixth, spring and winter clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Senior generals of the Left and Right Guards and below received six supplemental allowances: grain, salt, private horses, personal attendants, body servants, and spring and winter clothing.

sentences.zh: 私馬則有芻豆，手力則有資錢，隨身則有糧米、鹽，春冬服則有布、絹、絁、䌷、綿，射生、神策軍大將軍以下增以鞋，比大歷制祿又厚矣。

translations.literal: Private horses had fodder and beans; hand attendants had stipend money; personal guard had grain, rice, and salt; spring and winter clothing had cloth, silk, coarse silk, spun silk, and cotton; archer and Shence Army major generals and below were additionally given shoes—compared with the Dali system's salaries, again thicker.
translations.idiomatic: Horse allowances covered fodder; attendants drew cash; body servants received grain and salt; seasonal clothing included cloth, silk, and cotton; archers and Shence generals also got shoes—all more generous than the Dali schedule.

sentences.zh: 州縣官有手力雜給錢，然俸最薄者也。

translations.literal: Prefecture and county officials had hand-attendant miscellaneous grant money, yet their salaries were the thinnest.
translations.idiomatic: County officials received attendant allowances too, but their base pay remained the lowest in the system.

sentences.zh: 李泌以度支有兩稅錢，鹽鐵使有筦榷錢，可以擬經費，中外給用，每貫墊二十，號「戶部除陌錢」。

translations.literal: Li Bi, because the Revenue Bureau had two-tax money and the Salt and Iron Commissioner had monopoly money that could be matched to expenses, for domestic and foreign disbursements each string was shorted twenty cash, called 'Household Ministry coin-shaving money.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi funded domestic and foreign expenses from two-tax revenues and salt-monopoly receipts by shaving twenty cash from every string disbursed, a levy known as the Household Ministry discount fee.

sentences.zh: 復有闕官俸料、職田錢，積戶部，號「戶部別貯錢」。

translations.literal: There were also vacant-post salaries and office-land money accumulated at the Household Ministry, called 'Household Ministry separately stored money.'
translations.idiomatic: Salaries for unfilled posts and office-land proceeds were also pooled at the ministry under the name Household Ministry reserve fund.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞專掌之，皆以給京官，歲費不及五十五萬緡。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief exclusively managed it; all was used to supply capital officials; annual expense did not reach five hundred fifty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief controlled the reserve, which paid capital officials at an annual cost of less than 550,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 京兆和糴，度支給諸軍冬衣，亦往往取之。

translations.literal: Jingzhao grain purchases at fair price, and the Revenue Bureau's winter clothing for the armies, also often drew from it.
translations.idiomatic: The fund also routinely supplied Jingzhao grain purchases and army winter clothing from the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 減王公以下永業田：郡王、職事官從一品田五十頃，國公、職事官正二品田四十頃，郡公、職事官從二品田三十頃，縣公、職事官正四品田十四頃，職事官從四品田十一頃。

translations.literal: Hereditary allotments for princes and below were reduced: commandery princes and office-holding officials 1b, fifty qing; state dukes and office-holding officials 2a, forty qing; commandery dukes and office-holding officials 2b, thirty qing; county dukes and office-holding officials 4a, fourteen qing; office-holding officials 4b, eleven qing.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary land for princes and nobles was cut: commandery princes and associate first-rank officeholders to fifty qing, state dukes and second rank to forty, commandery dukes and associate second rank to thirty, county dukes and fourth rank to fourteen, and associate fourth rank to eleven.

sentences.zh: 尚郡主檢校四品京官者月給料錢三十萬，祿百二十石。

translations.literal: Those marrying a commandery princess and acting as fourth-rank capital officials were monthly given three hundred thousand cash stipend and one hundred twenty shi salary grain.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts of commandery princesses holding acting fourth-rank capital posts received three hundred thousand cash monthly and one hundred twenty shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 尚縣主檢校五品京官者料錢二十萬，祿百石。

translations.literal: Those marrying a county princess and acting as fifth-rank capital officials received two hundred thousand cash stipend and one hundred shi salary grain.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts of county princesses in acting fifth-rank capital posts drew two hundred thousand cash and one hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 自李泌增百官俸，當時以為不可朘削矣，然有名存而職廢、額去而俸在者。

translations.literal: Since Li Bi increased all officials' salaries, at the time it was thought they could not be reduced; yet there were cases where the name remained while the duty was abolished, the quota removed while the salary remained.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Bi's raise many believed salaries could never be cut again, yet titles lingered after duties vanished and pay continued after posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 宰相李吉甫建議減之，遂為常法。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Jifu proposed reducing them, and this became regular law.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Jifu proposed trimming such payments, and the reduction became permanent policy.

sentences.zh: 於時祠祭、蕃夷賜宴、別設，皆長安、萬年人吏主辦，二縣置本錢，配納質積戶收息以供費。

translations.literal: At the time state sacrifices, foreign banquets and gifts, and special arrangements were all managed by Chang'an and Wannian clerks; the two counties set up capital funds, assigned to quality storage households to collect interest to supply expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices, banquets for foreign envoys, and special entertainments were handled by clerks of Chang'an and Wannian, which seeded capital funds and assigned them to bonded warehouse keepers whose interest covered the costs.

sentences.zh: 諸使捉錢者，給牒免徭役，有罪府縣不敢劾治。

translations.literal: Money contractors of various commissioners were given documents exempting corvée; if guilty, prefectures and counties dared not investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners' money-lending agents carried exemption slips from corvée duty, and local magistrates dared not prosecute them even when they broke the law.

sentences.zh: 民間有不取本錢，立虛契，子孫相承為之。

translations.literal: Among the people there were those who did not take principal money but established empty contracts, descendants inheriting and continuing the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Some lenders never touched the principal but kept fictitious contracts that their heirs renewed generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 嘗有毆人破首，詣閑廄使納利錢受牒貸罪。

translations.literal: Once there was one who beat a man and broke his head; he went to the Stable Commissioner, paid interest money, received a document, and was pardoned for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: One man who beat another and cracked his skull paid interest to the Stable Commissioner, bought an exemption document, and escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞柳公綽奏諸使捉錢戶，府縣得捕役，給牒者毀之，自是不得錢者不納利矣。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Liu Gongchuo memorialized that money contractors of various commissioners could be impressed for corvée by prefectures and counties; those given documents should have them destroyed; from then on those who could not pay did not pay interest.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Liu Gongchuo ruled that commissioners' lenders could be drafted for corvée, their exemption slips voided, and from then on the indigent owed no interest.

sentences.zh: 議者以兩省、尚書省、御史臺總樞機，正百寮，而倍稱息利，非馭官之體。

translations.literal: Critics held that the Two Departments, Ministry of Revenue, and Censorate controlled the pivot of government and corrected the hundred officials, yet doubled interest rates—this was not the proper way to manage officials.
translations.idiomatic: Critics protested that the Secretariat, Chancellery, Ministry, and Censorate—the organs that governed the bureaucracy—should not themselves charge usurious rates.

sentences.zh: 元和九年，戶部除陌錢每緡增墊五錢，四時給諸司諸使之餐，置驅使官督之，御史一人核其侵漁，起明年正月，收息五之一，號「元和十年新收置公廨本錢」。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanhe, the Household Ministry coin-shaving fee each string was increased by five cash shaved; four seasons supplied meals for various bureaus and commissioners; driving officials were established to supervise; one censor audited embezzlement; starting next year's first month, one-fifth interest was collected, called 'Yuanhe tenth-year newly established office-capital funds.'
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 9 (814) the discount fee rose by five cash per string to fund seasonal meals for agencies and commissioners under supervising clerks and a censor's audit; from the following first month one-fifth interest was collected on a fund called the Yuanhe 10 office-capital reserve.

sentences.zh: 初，捉錢者私增公廨本，以防耗失，而富人乘以為奸，可督者私之，外以逋官錢迫蹙閭裏，民不堪其擾。

translations.literal: Initially, money contractors privately increased office capital to guard against loss, but wealthy men multiplied this as fraud; those who could be collected upon privatized it, outwardly pressing neighborhoods with delinquent official money; the people could not bear the harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Contractors had padded office capital against losses, but the rich turned the practice into extortion, privatizing recoverable debts and squeezing neighborhoods for delinquent official loans until the populace could endure no more.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞崔從奏增錢者不得逾官本。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Cui Cong memorialized that increased funds must not exceed official capital.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Cui Cong ruled that private additions could not exceed the official principal.

sentences.zh: 其後兩省捉錢，官給牒逐利江淮之間，鬻茶鹽以橈法。

translations.literal: Afterward the Two Departments' money contractors, with official documents given, sought profit between the Yangtze and Huai, selling tea and salt to circumvent the law.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Two Departments sent licensed lenders into the Jianghuai region to trade tea and salt in violation of monopoly law.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以職田多少不均，每司收草粟以多少為差。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, because office land was uneven in amount, each bureau collected grass and grain according to the difference in quantity.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 13 (818) uneven office-land holdings led each agency to collect fodder grain in proportion to its acreage.

sentences.zh: 其後宰相李玨、楊嗣復奏堂廚食利錢擾民煩碎，於是罷堂廚捉錢官，置庫量入計費。

translations.literal: Afterward chancellors Li Jue and Yang Sifu memorialized that hall-kitchen interest money harassed the people with trivial matters; therefore hall-kitchen money contractors were abolished and a treasury established to measure income and calculate expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Li Jue and Yang Sifu later reported that the chancellery kitchen's lending agents burdened the people with petty exactions; the agents were abolished and a treasury set up on a strict budget.

sentences.zh: 唐世百官俸錢，會昌後不復增減，今著其數：太師、太傅、太保，錢二百萬。

translations.literal: Tang-era hundred officials' salary money, after Huichang no longer increased or decreased; now the figures are recorded: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector, two million cash.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huichang era (841-846) Tang official salaries were fixed without further change; the schedule reads: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector, two million cash each.

sentences.zh: 太尉、司徒、司空，百六十萬。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal, Minister of Education, Minister of Works, one million six hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works, 1.6 million cash.

sentences.zh: 侍中，百五十萬。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, one million five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant, 1.5 million cash.

sentences.zh: 中書令，門下中書侍郎，左右仆射，太子太師、太保、太傅，百四十萬。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat, Secretariat and Chancellery Vice Ministers, Left and Right Vice Directors, Crown Prince Grand Preceptor, Grand Protector, Grand Tutor, one million four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat, vice ministers of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Left and Right Vice Directors, and the crown prince's Grand Preceptor, Grand Protector, and Grand Tutor, 1.4 million cash.

sentences.zh: 尚書，御史大夫，太子少師、少保、少傅，百萬。

translations.literal: Ministers, Censor-in-Chief, Crown Prince Junior Preceptor, Junior Protector, Junior Tutor, one million.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers, the Censor-in-Chief, and the crown prince's Junior Preceptor, Junior Protector, and Junior Tutor, one million cash.

sentences.zh: 節度使，三十萬。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner, three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner, three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 都防禦使、副使，監軍，十五萬。

translations.literal: Regional Defense Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Army Supervisor, one hundred fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Defense Commissioner and deputy, and army supervisor, one hundred fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 觀察使十萬。

translations.literal: Observation Commissioner, one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Observation Commissioner, one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 左右丞，侍郎，散騎常侍，諫議大夫，給事中，中書舍人，秘書、殿中、內侍監，御史中丞，太常、宗正、大理、司農、太府、鴻臚、太仆、光祿、衛尉卿，國子祭酒，將作、少府監，太子賓客、詹事，諸府尹，大都督府長史，都團練使、副使，上州刺史，八萬。

translations.literal: Left and Right Assistant Directors, Vice Ministers, Regular Attendant Cavalier, Remonstrance Grand Masters, Drafting Attendants, Secretariat Drafters, Directors of the Secretariat Archive, Palace Administration, and Inner Palace Service, Censor-in-Chief, Directors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Imperial Clan, Court of Judicial Review, Agriculture, Grand Treasury, Court of State Ceremonial, Imperial Stud, Court of Imperial Commissary, Court of Imperial Guards, Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, Directors of Imperial Construction and the Palace Workshops, Crown Prince Guest and Household Superintendent, prefects of various prefectures, chief administrators of superior area commands, regional training commissioners and deputies, upper-grade prefects, eighty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Assistant Directors, vice ministers, palace attendants, remonstrance officials, drafting attendants, secretariat drafters, archive and palace directors, the censor-in-chief, the nine ministry directors, the imperial academy chancellor, construction and workshop directors, crown prince staff, metropolitan prefects, area-command administrators, regional training commissioners and deputies, and upper-grade prefects, eighty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 太常、宗正少卿，太子左右庶子，節度副使，刺史知軍事，七萬。

translations.literal: Vice Directors of Imperial Sacrifices and Imperial Clan, Crown Prince Left and Right Assistant Superintendents, Military Commissioner Deputies, Prefects Managing Military Affairs, seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors of the Sacrifices and Imperial Clan courts, crown prince assistants, military commissioner deputies, and prefects with military command, seventy thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 六軍統軍，諸府少尹，少監，少卿，國子司業，少詹事，六萬五千。

translations.literal: Commanders of the Six Armies, deputy prefects of various prefectures, deputy directors, vice directors, Imperial Academy Vice Chancellor, deputy household superintendent, sixty-five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders of the Six Armies, deputy prefects, deputy directors and vice directors, the academy vice chancellor, and deputy crown prince stewards, sixty-five thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 左右衛、金吾衛上將軍，六軍大將軍，六萬。

translations.literal: Left and Right Guard and Golden Crow Guard senior generals, Six Armies major generals, sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Senior generals of the Left and Right Guards and Golden Crow Guard and major generals of the Six Armies, sixty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 左右驍衛、武衛、威衛、領軍衛、監門衛、千牛衛上將軍，上州別駕，五萬五千。

translations.literal: Left and Right Valiant, Martial, Majestic, Army-leading, Gate-inspecting, and Thousand-Ox Guard senior generals, upper-grade prefect vice administrators, fifty-five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Senior generals of the remaining palace guards and vice administrators of upper-grade prefectures, fifty-five thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 郎中，司天監，太子左右諭德、家令寺、仆寺、率更寺令，親王傅，別敕判官，觀察、團練判官掌書記，上州長史、司馬，五萬。
